title: Review: Sigma/pi, hybridisation and resonance; formal charge; Carbocation stability and Markovnikov; Addition polymers and disposal; Alcohols: production, dehydration and halogenation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR13#t1 term and clue written for the game; BD07#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR13#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR16#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BD07#N.5, OR13#N.6, OR14#N.5, OR16#N.18c, BD07#N.13, OR13#N.3, OR14#N.3, OR16#N.17, OR13#N.8b, OR14#N.16, OR16#N.16, OR13#N.9. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Unsymmetrical alkene
items.clue: Its two C=C carbons carry different groups, so HBr can add in two ways, as with propene.

items.label: Sigma bond
items.clue: Direct, head-on overlap of orbitals, with electron density on the axis between the nuclei.

items.label: Primary carbocation
items.clue: The least stable type of C⁺ species, with only one alkyl group bonded to the charged atom.

items.label: Leaving group
items.clue: What departs as the C–O bond breaks: OH⁻ is a poor one, but a neutral H₂O molecule is stable.

questions.stem: A student suggests that a π bond between two carbon atoms prevents rotation about the bond that joins them. Which observation does this hypothesis predict?

options.text: ClHC=CHCl exists as two separable compounds
ClH₂C–CH₂Cl exists as two separable compounds
H₂C=CHCl exists as two separable compounds
ClC≡CCl exists as two separable compounds

questions.explanation: With no rotation, the two Cl atoms are fixed on the same side or opposite sides of C=C: two isomers. ClH₂C–CH₂Cl has no π bond, so it rotates and is one compound.

questions.stem: 2-methylbut-1-ene, CH₂=C(CH₃)CH₂CH₃, reacts with hydrogen bromide. What is the major product, and why?

options.text: 1-bromo-2-methylbutane, as it forms via a tertiary carbocation
2-bromo-2-methylbutane, as it forms via a tertiary carbocation
2-bromo-2-methylbutane, as Br adds to the carbon that has more H atoms
1-bromo-2-methylbutane, as the primary carbocation is less crowded, so it forms faster

questions.explanation: H adds to the CH₂ end (C1). The C⁺ on C2 has three alkyl groups: tertiary, the most stable. Br⁻ bonds to it: CH₃CBr(CH₃)CH₂CH₃.

questions.stem: A section of an addition polymer is –CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–. Which is the monomer?

options.text: (CH₃)₃CH
CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃
(CH₃)₃COH
(CH₃)₂C=CH₂

questions.explanation: The repeating unit is –CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–. Restoring the C=C between the two main-chain carbons gives (CH₃)₂C=CH₂, 2-methylpropene.

questions.stem: Butan-1-ol is reacted separately with sodium, with hydrogen bromide and with phosphorus pentachloride. In which reaction does the O–H bond break while the C–O bond stays intact?

options.text: With hydrogen bromide
With sodium
With phosphorus pentachloride
In all three reactions

questions.explanation: 2CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂O⁻Na⁺ + H₂. The O stays on the carbon; only the O–H hydrogen is replaced.

questions.stem: Mean (average) bond enthalpies: C–C 347 kJ mol⁻¹ · C=C 612 kJ mol⁻¹ · C≡C 838 kJ mol⁻¹. A C≡C bond is only about 2.4 times as strong as a C–C bond, not 3 times. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Its three shared pairs repel one another, so C≡C is longer than C–C.
All three of its bonds are σ bonds, but they are weaker because they share space.
Two of its three bonds come from sideways overlap of p orbitals, which is less effective.
Its π electrons lie on the axis between the nuclei, where σ electrons repel them.

questions.explanation: C≡C is one σ and two π. Each π adds less than a σ: 612 − 347 = 265, then 838 − 612 = 226. So the total is well below 3 × 347 = 1041.

questions.stem: Which carbocation is the most stable?

options.text: CH₃⁺
CH₃CH₂CH₂⁺
CH₃CH⁺CH₃
(CH₃)₃C⁺

questions.explanation: This is tertiary: three alkyl groups on the positive carbon. Tertiary carbocations are the most stable.

questions.stem: Propene, CH₂=CHCH₃, forms the addition polymer poly(propene), written as [repeating unit]ₙ. Which option gives the repeating unit and describes it correctly?

options.text: –CH₂=CH(CH₃)–, keeping each monomer's C=C
–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–, one unit of a single long chain
–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–, all three carbons in the main chain
CH₃CH₂CH₃, one of n separate small molecules

questions.explanation: One bond of each C=C breaks and the two former C=C carbons form the main chain, with CH₃ as a side group. [–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–]ₙ represents one chain containing n of these units.

questions.stem: A few drops of an unknown colourless liquid are added to solid PCl₅. Steamy fumes appear. What can you conclude?

options.text: The liquid must be an alcohol.
The fumes are chlorine gas.
The liquid contains a C=C bond.
The liquid contains an O–H group.

questions.explanation: PCl₅ swaps the OH for Cl and releases HCl, which fumes in moist air. Alcohols, acids and water all do this.

questions.stem: 2-methylpropene, (CH₃)₂C=CH₂, reacts with hydrogen bromide. What is the minor product, and which carbocation does it form through?

options.text: 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, via a tertiary carbocation
1-bromo-2-methylpropane, via a tertiary carbocation
1-bromo-2-methylpropane, via a primary carbocation
1,2-dibromo-2-methylpropane, via a secondary carbocation

questions.explanation: If H adds to the central carbon, C⁺ is on the CH₂ end: (CH₃)₂CHCH₂⁺, primary. This slow route gives the minor product, (CH₃)₂CHCH₂Br.

questions.stem: Poly(propene) can be heated until soft, moulded into a new shape, and cooled. The same plastic can be remoulded many times, and its chemical properties do not change. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Heating breaks C–C bonds in the chains, and new C–C bonds form in the new positions on cooling.
Heating turns the chains back into propene molecules, which polymerise again as the plastic cools.
Heating overcomes the forces between chains, which re-form on cooling; no covalent bonds break.
Heating breaks the covalent bonds between neighbouring chains, and these re-form on cooling.

questions.stem: Propan-2-ol is warmed with potassium bromide and sulfuric acid. What is the main organic product?

options.text: 2-bromopropane
1-bromopropane
Propene
2-bromopropan-2-ol

questions.explanation: Br replaces the OH on the same carbon: CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ + HBr → CH₃CHBrCH₃ + H₂O.

questions.stem: 1-methylcyclohexene is a six-membered ring with one C=C. One C=C carbon carries a CH₃ group and no H; the other carries one H. It reacts with hydrogen bromide. What is the major product, and why?

options.text: 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane, as H adds to the CH carbon of the C=C, giving a tertiary carbocation
1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane, as H adds to the carbon carrying the CH₃ group, giving a tertiary carbocation
1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane, as Br goes to the carbon with more space around it
Equal amounts of both, as the ring makes both carbons of the C=C equivalent

questions.explanation: With H on the CH carbon, C⁺ is on the ring carbon bearing CH₃: three alkyl groups, tertiary. Br⁻ bonds there, so Br and CH₃ share a carbon.
